posts.author: elonmusk
posts.text:
SpaceX is building a supercomputer near Brownsville, Texas.

The first job on site was cleaning up sixty years of other people's trash.

Scrap metal, rusting tanks, old appliances and thousands of illegal tires, hauled out of the mud.

Think about that for a second.

This site will train frontier AI for medical research, emergency response, advanced manufacturing and national security.

It will make its own electricity, so the neighbors' power bills stay their own.

SpaceX is also putting $220 million into Brownsville's water and wastewater system, adding 20 million gallons of capacity every day for the city.

More than 3,000 construction jobs already, with more than 500 permanent ones to come.

Elon Musk summed it up in three words: "SpaceX community benefits."

A company spends $15 billion on Starship and another $24 billion on a supercomputer in one corner of Texas when it plans to stay for decades.

Elon Musk builds the place up first, because he believes the future will be built right there.

quote.author: SpaceX
quote.name: SpaceX
quote.text:
Development of the Starbase supercompute site is creating an opportunity to address decades of environmental neglect. 

Portions of the property were used for unauthorized dumping dating back to the 1960s. We're undertaking cleanup efforts to remove decades of accumulated debris, including scrap metal, discarded appliances, old tanks, fiberglass insulation, construction materials, and thousands of illegally dumped tires

These are the community benefits if @SpaceX builds their planned $50 billion Arizona Supercomputing Campus:

• 6,500 jobs (1,000 permanent, 5,500 construction).
• Up to $103M annually in new property tax revenue.
• 10-40% lower electricity bills projected for local SSVEC residential customers.
• Up to $250M in one-time county sales tax revenue.
• Up to $460M annually in additional benefits for Arizona electric cooperative members.
• $3.6B in grid upgrades funded by SpaceX at no cost to cooperative members.
• 24 GWh of battery storage to improve grid stability and reliability.
• Additional solar energy to reduce strain on the local grid.
• Minimal water usage, with no new wells and zero ongoing industrial water consumption projected.
• Aquifer and wildlife protection, including conservation initiatives.
• Reduced noise and light pollution through noise mitigation and dark-sky protections.
• Support for local schools, infrastructure, businesses, and essential services.

quote.author: SawyerMerritt
quote.name: Sawyer Merritt
quote.text:
SpaceX has just unveiled a massive new $50 billion Supercomputing Campus that they want to build in Cochise County, Arizona.

All info:
• Up to 6 GW across the 9 supercomputing buildings
• Construction starts 2027
• Size of each supercomputing building: ~493,000 square feet.
• Total supercomputing building space: 4.44 million square feet, excluding support facilities.
• SSVEC residential customers are projected to see electricity bill reductions of 10–40%.
• Up to 24 GWh of grid-connected battery storage to provide backup power, stabilize the regional electric grid, support local voltage, and absorb fluctuations in electricity demand. Among the largest planned battery installations in the United States.
• Additional solar generation in the region is planned to supply renewable electricity during the day and reduce demand on the local grid.
• No dedicated on-site power plant or fuel storage yard is planned.
• Each supercomputing building will have 10 MW of natural-gas-powered standby generation for critical equipment, operating only during utility outages and periodic testing.
• No gas turbines will be installed at the site.
• SpaceX plans to fund $3.6 billion in grid infrastructure upgrades, transferred to AEPCO at no cost to its members.
• Up to $260 million annually in additional benefits for cooperative members at full buildout, on top of residential bill reductions.
• Up to $200 million annually for cooperative members statewide, in addition to SSVEC benefits.
• The supercomputers will use dry cooling with a closed-loop water circulation system rather than evaporative cooling.
• SpaceX projects zero ongoing industrial water consumption.
• The cooling system will be filled initially, with water reused for up to 10 years.
• SpaceX estimates annual water usage equivalent to approximately 20–30 Arizona residential homes.
• Projected annual water use would be less than 2.5% of a single center-pivot irrigation system's annual consumption.
• Permanent jobs: Approximately 1,000.
• Construction jobs: Approximately 5,500.
• Annual property tax revenue: Up to $103 million in estimated new annual revenue.
• Regional economic benefits: SpaceX says its investment will support public education, infrastructure, essential local services, and economic development.
• Local suppliers: SpaceX is encouraging suppliers to participate in construction and development of the campus.
• Noise mitigation: Equipment will be positioned away from neighboring properties where possible, with setbacks and additional screening to reduce noise.
• Nighttime lighting: Outdoor lighting will remain off unless work is underway, with active lights shielded and directed downward.
• Dark-sky protection: The campus will comply with Cochise County's dark-sky requirements to limit light pollution.
• Nighttime construction: SpaceX says it will seek waivers when nighttime construction lighting is necessary.
• Wildlife protection: The campus is being designed with consideration for the region's sandhill crane wintering habitat.

This campus's purpose is to build one of the world's most advanced AI supercomputing campuses to train SpaceX's superintelligence models and support scientific and engineering breakthroughs.

Learn more: https://www.spacex.com/sites/cochise-county

posts.text:
Why Elon Musk believes we could colonize the entire galaxy in a million years

To Elon Musk, it's not even a hard question.

A million years is enough to spread across the whole galaxy.

So where is everyone?

Nobody seems to have done it.

Something stops civilizations before they get out there. That's the great filter.

And it's why he thinks about Mars with one specific test.

Elon: "Do we have enough resources on Mars such that if the spaceships from Earth stopped coming, you can survive?"

Joe Rogan compared it to a long sea voyage where the only thing you're missing is vitamin C.

And the ships could stop for reasons that aren't dramatic at all.

Civilization on Earth could end with a bang or a whimper.

A Mars that can survive on its own is how he thinks we get past the filter. https://x.com/NarutoNolimits/status/2087243319604867404/video/1

quote.author: bowie_HQ
quote.name: Bowie
quote.text:
2015, Colbert: “You’re a billionaire trying to do good things. Superhero or supervillain? You have to choose one.”

Elon: shows him a robot snake that plugs itself into your car

Colbert: “Is that thing going to attack me in my sleep?”

Elon, completely deadpan: “For the prototype, at least, I would recommend not dropping anything when you’re near it.”

Ten years later he’s built reusable rockets, humanoid robots and the best-selling EV on the planet, and he’s still the only CEO who can deliver a product safety warning and a punchline in the same sentence.

Superhero, obviously. Just one with a very dry sense of humor.

@elonmusk
